title: Reserve Bank of India — National Financial Literacy Curriculum Guidelines
summary: Core guidelines from the Reserve Bank of India on household budgeting, emergency reserve buffers, disciplined savings, and digital payment safety.

chunks.title: Prudent Household Cash Flow and Emergency Reserve Buffer
chunks.text: The Reserve Bank of India Financial Education initiative emphasizes establishing an emergency reserve fund covering at least 3 to 6 months of mandatory living expenses (rent, utility bills, food supplies, insurance premiums, and loan EMIs). Emergency funds must be kept in liquid or near-liquid instruments such as savings bank accounts, sweep-in fixed deposits, or liquid mutual funds. Users must never allocate emergency reserves to speculative or illiquid assets.

chunks.title: Responsible Credit Utilization and Debt-to-Income Discipline
chunks.text: RBI consumer protection guidance recommends that total monthly debt service obligations—including home loan EMIs, auto loans, personal loans, and credit card minimum dues—should strictly not exceed 40% to 50% of monthly net disposable income (Fixed Obligation to Income Ratio or FOIR). Carrying revolving credit card debt at high annual percentage rates (typically 36% to 45% per annum) causes compounding financial distress and should be prioritized for immediate retirement.

chunks.title: Systematic Savings and Discretionary Spending Control
chunks.text: The basic rule of disciplined personal finance advised by RBI financial inclusion programs is: 'Income minus Planned Savings equals Permissible Expenditure', rather than saving whatever remains after spending. Consumers should automate systematic monthly savings on their salary credit day prior to incurring non-essential lifestyle expenditures.
